current_answer: Real money for agent-assisted work reaches humans: on HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Kaggle, Algora and Upwork the owner holds the account, passes identity checks, validates and submits the work, and withdraws, and none of the six human-paying venues with confirmed payouts allows autonomous submission in its quoted terms. Agent-first boards pay agents on-chain, but little: in the 30 days to 4 October 2026 we traced $223.74 paid to agent workers, 37.85% of it from operator or operator-linked wallets, with one identified independent payer (MolTrust, $11.25, promotional) and no venue at meaningful scale. Selling per call over x402 shows more unlinked money than the boards, but traced buyers show the raw buyer counts overstate independent customers, and no agent-work x402 seller is confirmed at meaningful scale. Human-account bounty work is the only route with plainly independent payers, at an unknown rate for AI-assisted work. Agent communities are not paid work: of 17 measured on 4 October, 6 are active and 4 of those pass without a flag or caveat (Moltbook, The Colony, Agent4Science, OpenClawCity); no community token has a payout route, and we would let an agent join only Moltbook or The Colony with controls, or Agent4Science or cq for a specific purpose.

catalogue_card.question: Where can AI agents actually get paid for real work?
catalogue_card.text: Humans who use agents get real payouts on bug bounties and competitions, but no human-paying venue allows autonomous submission. Agent-first boards paid agent workers $223.74 in 30 days, 38% from operators or linked wallets. Per-call x402 selling shows more unlinked money, but no agent-work seller is confirmed at scale. Agent communities: 6 of 17 active, none pays. All routes untested by this pool.

summary: Agent communities (4 October 2026): 17 communities and community-like sites measured. 6 meet the active bar (newest item under 48 h, at least 10 distinct authors, at least 5 items a day): Moltbook, The Colony, Agent4Science, 4claw, Clawstr and OpenClawCity. 3 are low activity (cq, AgentDiscuss, Moltter), 5 inactive (LobChan and Agent Commune provisionally) and 3 speculative.

Only 4 active communities pass with no concentration flag and no caveat: Moltbook, The Colony, Agent4Science and OpenClawCity. Clawstr is active only on paper (256 of 264 pubkeys posted once; top pubkey 44%); 4claw rests on a partial HTML sample; Moltter is flagged (2 accounts wrote every post).

Should my agent join? Join with controls: Moltbook, The Colony. Join for a purpose: Agent4Science (research review), cq (coding knowledge). Wait: 4claw, Clawstr, OpenClawCity, Chirper.ai, AgentDiscuss, Moltter, xfor.bot. Do not join: MoltX, ClawNews, LobChan, Agent Commune, the moltsbooks.com lookalike, and the Agents4Science 2025 conference. Join steps are untested by the pool.

No community pays for work and no community token has a payout route; the CLAWSTR contract is confirmed on-chain but its official status is disputed, and MOLT and LAUKI are ambiguous. 2 sites have a wallet step (Clawstr, Chirper.ai).

Safety: 2,030 sampled community items held 18 injection-shaped matches (16 benign mentions, 1 discussion, 1 post aimed at agents, 0 key-seeking); our 1 in 2,030 (about 0.05%) sits next to Vectra's secondary 2.6% Moltbook estimate, by a different method. New observed designs: sec-14 (Clawstr unpinned npm package and wallet), sec-15 (Agent4Science verifier code), sec-16 (OpenClawCity server-sent shell script and background process).

Ledger: $223.74 reached agent workers in the 30 days to 4 October 2026 (3 October: $230.83, mostly window roll-off); 37.85% came from operator or operator-linked wallets (range 29.3% to 42.3%); 1 identified independent payer, MolTrust, $11.25, promotional, whose 40 newest awards all went to the same 10 addresses; 0 venues at meaningful scale.

Six agent-first boards re-checked on 4 October: no E-level changed. dealwork.ai withdrawals: Stripe Connect bank payout or USDC, minimum $10, crypto withdrawals admin-reviewed, owner session required.

x402 refresh: Cluster Protocol showed no inbound USDC since 2026-10-02T12:00Z (observed, not concluded); new StableEnrich and OneShot buyers are operator-linked; AX1's flatter distribution is funded by one wallet. Still no agent-work x402 seller with at least 5 unlinked or identified buyers.
Rules: 65 key rows re-checked on 4 October, 0 changed (3 Kaggle rows unfetchable; TaskMarket terms still a draft); 16 rows added, 15 from community terms, for 170 in all. Not legal advice.
Homepage counts unchanged: 26 paid-work or selling venues, 12 with a confirmed payout (E1), 5 paying agent-performed work (4 in the last 30 days), 0 with an independent payer at meaningful scale.
uncertainty: Community statuses rest on one dated sample each. Clawstr's author count is likely inflated, 4claw's sample is a partial HTML read with display names as authors, cq is measured on its code repository only, and LobChan and Agent Commune are inactive on a single day's reading (provisional).

Community join steps come from the sites' own documents and were not tested. Token ties: official status is disputed or unknown unless the operator says otherwise; on-chain data alone never makes a tie official.
Our community scan rate (1 in 2,030) and Vectra's 2.6% Moltbook estimate use different methods and are not comparable; a low match rate is not proof of safety.

On-chain data proves transfers, not identities: unlinked means no link was found within two hops, not independence. If funder 0xd8c5763b (80.6% of TaskMarket gross, unidentified) is operator-affiliated, the ledger operator share rises to about 85%. Virtuals ACP's class split is apportioned from a 1 October sample, hence the 29.3% to 42.3% range.

Cluster Protocol's x402 stop since 2026-10-02T12:00Z is observed, not concluded: it may be a pause, a payTo change or an indexing gap. x402 buyer samples are hours long for most sellers; 30-day estimates are extrapolations. AX1's funder 0x3dd6f35c pattern does not prove common ownership.

No primary source gives a dollar figure for bounties paid on AI-assisted findings. The 5 HackerOne programme policy rows, three Kaggle rows and Google VRP are unverified snippets. CDP facilitator seller KYC: no requirement found, not ruled out.
Rule verdicts describe the quoted text, not enforcement, and are not legal advice. TaskMarket's terms page is still a draft that is "not approved or active".
No pathway, walkthrough or community join was tested by the pool; no account was opened, no wallet signed, no payment header built and no job taken.
freshness_note: Communities measured 4 October 2026, about 13:40 to 14:00 UTC; ledger covers 4 September to 4 October 2026 (to 13:45 UTC); x402 buyer distributions refreshed 4 October; 65 key rule rows re-checked 4 October; 20 venue records re-checked 4 October, others 3 October or earlier. Terms, statuses and communities change often; treat any record older than about 60 days as stale.
